settings.cohort_selection: First N lexicographically sorted case IDs, or all 147 if no limit
settings.throughput_definition: Full nnUNetv2_predict process from launch through exit after saved masks, including Python startup, model loading, preprocessing, prediction and mask export. Output verification is outside the timer. Batch wall time / case count is throughput, not individual-image latency.
settings.single_case_definition: Independent process-cold CLI timing of the first sorted case. Filesystem cache state is uncontrolled.
settings.latency_definition: Synchronized predict_logits_from_preprocessed_data call, including transfers, state-dict loading and CPU accumulation inside that call. Model initialization, preprocessing and mask export are excluded. Warm-up cases are discarded, then included in every measured repeat.
settings.parent_memory_definition: resource.RUSAGE_SELF lifetime high-water RSS, sampled after latency, including model and preloaded/preprocessed images. Not a batch-child or accelerator peak-memory measurement.
settings.process_tree_memory_scope: Sampled sum of RSS for the prediction subprocess and its recursive children only; excludes the benchmark parent. Shared pages can be counted more than once and short-lived peaks or children can be missed. This is not accelerator peak memory.
settings.process_tree_memory_unavailable_reason: psutil is not installed; no parent RSS substitute

settings.notes: inference_seconds covers only predict_logits_from_preprocessed_data (the sliding-window predictor call), synchronized when device is cuda or mps. It includes any host-device transfers and CPU-side accumulation inside that call, not just accelerator kernel time. Preprocessing (file I/O, resampling, normalization) and export are excluded from inference_seconds and timed separately where applicable. Peak CUDA allocation is measured after warm-up and excludes non-PyTorch VRAM. Peak CPU RSS is the benchmark process high-water mark, including preloaded images, not the separate batch-prediction process. Model loading time is measured separately and excludes the one-time host-to-device weight transfer, which occurs during the discarded warm-up pass. To replicate on another device, rerun this script with the same --checkpoint, --dataset-name, --fold, --seeds, --step-size, worker counts, repeats and --disable-mirroring settings recorded here, changing only --device and --output-dir.

limitations: Cross-system comparison: hardware, OS, software builds and host CPUs differ; not a controlled device-only experiment.
Thread settings differ across devices and between configured and inside-predictor CPU counts; see device settings. Archived CUDA interop/batch thread counts are not recorded.
Backend autocast/precision is not recorded in these settings; CPU-side accumulation and host-device transfers are inside the predictor call, so latency is not kernel-only time.
Predictor latency excludes preprocessing/export; full-batch wall time includes startup, loading, preprocessing and saved-mask export. Cold start is process-cold, not cache-cold.

Unequal throughput repeats: CPU=3, MPS=3, CUDA=1. Archived CUDA has only one run; no CUDA repeat SD or repeat-based speedup confidence interval is estimable. Latency spread describes cases, not independent runs.
Power-state, thermal state, background load and filesystem cache are not verified by these artifacts; no power-state telemetry is recorded.

Memory scopes differ: parent lifetime high-water RSS includes preloaded images; child process-tree RSS is separate and unavailable locally without psutil; CUDA allocation excludes non-PyTorch VRAM. These are not comparable total-memory peaks.
Local energy was not measured. Whole-command CUDA telemetry has no comparable local/per-phase energy measurement; energy efficiency cannot be inferred from TDP or timing.
Local checkpoint hashes agree with trusted metadata; archived CUDA records checkpoint size/selection, not a checkpoint hash. CUDA cold-start timing is unavailable.
Quantiles use NumPy linear interpolation and SD uses ddof=1; casewise speedup is baseline/device and delta is device-baseline, using per-case means over latency repeats.
